target: 신랑이 많이 긴장한 것 같았어요.
english: The groom seemed very nervous.
tip: In a guess the tense lives on 같다 (gatda = seem): 긴장한 것 같았어요 (ginjanghan geot gatasseoyo) = it seemed he was nervous – 같았어요 is past because the seeming was then.

target: 주례 선생님의 말씀이 정말 감동적이었어요.
english: The officiant's words were really moving.
tip: 말씀 (malsseum) = honored 'words/speech' of an elder.

target: 두 분이 오래오래 행복하시길 바라요.
english: I hope the two live happily for a long time.
tip: 행복하시길 바라요 (haengbokhasigil barayo): the -시- inside honors the couple being wished well, while plain 바라요 (barayo = I hope) is your own act – no honoring yourself.

target: 다음 주에 좋아하는 가수의 콘서트에 가요.
english: I'm going to my favorite singer's concert next week.
tip: Verbs sit in front of nouns like adjectives: 좋아하는 가수 (joahaneun gasu) = 'the liking singer', i.e. the singer I like. English puts the clause after; Korean packs it before, with -는.

target: 콘서트 표가 십 분 만에 다 매진됐어요.
english: The concert tickets all sold out in ten minutes.
tip: 만에 after a time span = 'in only that long': 십 분 만에 (sip bun mane) = in just ten minutes. It carries the surprise at the speed – the tickets vanished that fast.

target: 새 앨범이 나오자마자 바로 샀어요.
english: I bought the new album as soon as it came out.
tip: -자마자 means 'as soon as' with zero gap: 나오자마자 (naojamaja) = the instant it came out. The two actions touch – no time allowed between release and purchase.

target: 그 가수는 춤과 노래를 둘 다 잘해요.
english: That singer is good at both dancing and singing.
tip: 'And' between nouns picks its shape by sound: 와 (wa) after vowels, 과 (gwa) after consonants. 춤 (chum) ends in a consonant, so it's 춤과 노래 (chumgwa norae) = dance and song.

target: 콘서트에서 앙코르를 세 곡이나 했어요.
english: They did as many as three encore songs.
tip: 세 곡이나 (se gogina) isn't just 'three songs' – the -이나 adds surprise at the amount: 'three whole songs!'. Drop it and the number turns neutral.

target: 콘서트가 끝나고도 한참 여운이 남았어요.
english: The feeling lingered long after the concert ended.
tip: 여운이 남았어요 (yeouni namasseoyo): 여운 is literally the lingering sound after a note ends, and 남다 (namda) = remain. Korean says the concert's echo stayed behind.

target: 저는 데뷔 때부터 그들을 계속 응원했어요.
english: I've supported them ever since their debut.
tip: -부터 (buteo) marks the starting point: 데뷔 때부터 (debwi ttaebuteo) = from the time of their debut. 때 (ttae = time) plus -부터 builds 'ever since' for any event.

target: 친구가 사인회에 같이 가자고 했어요.
english: A friend suggested we go to a signing event together.
tip: Reported 'let's' has its own ending: -자고 하다. 가자고 했어요 (gajago haesseoyo) = said 'let's go' – the 자 (ja) carries the suggestion, so no quotation marks needed.

target: 무대 위의 그 가수가 정말 멋있었어요.
english: That singer on stage was really cool.
tip: Korean location words are nouns: 무대 위 (mudae wi) = 'the stage's top'. With -의 (ui) it modifies the next noun: 무대 위의 가수 (mudae wiui gasu) = the on-stage singer.

target: 저는 노래방에서 케이팝을 자주 불러요.
english: I often sing K-pop at the karaoke room.
tip: 방 (bang = room) builds venues: 노래방 (noraebang) = song-room, i.e. karaoke. The same pattern gives PC방 (PC-bang, internet cafe) and 찜질방 (jjimjilbang, sauna).

target: 열성 팬들이 가수를 위해 기부도 해요.
english: Devoted fans even donate for their singer.
tip: 를 위해 (reul wihae) = 'for the sake of': 가수를 위해 (gasureul wihae) = for their singer. It marks who benefits – stronger and more deliberate than plain 'for'.

target: 어제 친구랑 극장에 영화를 보러 갔어요.
english: Yesterday I went to the cinema with a friend to see a movie.
tip: Purpose of movement gets its own ending: 보러 갔어요 (boreo gasseoyo) = went in order to watch. -(으)러 only attaches to going/coming verbs – it states why you moved.

target: 그 영화는 실화를 바탕으로 만들었어요.
english: That movie was based on a true story.
tip: 바탕 (batang) = base or foundation: 실화를 바탕으로 (silhwareul batangeuro) = 'with a true story as the base'. That's how Korean says 'based on' – the source is the ground under it.

target: 이 드라마는 요즘 젊은 사람들한테 인기가 많아요.
english: This drama is very popular with young people these days.
tip: You don't 'be popular' in Korean – you have lots of popularity: 인기가 많아요 (ingiga manayo), literally 'popularity is plentiful'. Popularity is a possession, not a trait.

target: 영화관에서 팝콘을 사서 먹었어요.
english: I bought popcorn at the cinema and ate it.
tip: 사서 먹었어요 (saseo meogeosseoyo) = bought it and ate that very popcorn – -아/어서 keeps the first action's result in hand. Plain -고 would just list two separate acts.

target: 저는 주말에 그 드라마를 밤새 몰아서 봤어요.
english: I binge-watched that drama all night on the weekend.
tip: 몰다 (molda) = to herd or drive together: 몰아서 봤어요 (moraseo bwasseoyo) = watched them herded into one sitting. Korean binge-watching literally rounds the episodes up.

target: 저는 감동적인 영화를 보면 자주 울어요.
english: I often cry when I watch moving movies.
tip: -적인 turns idea-nouns into adjectives: 감동 (gamdong = deep emotion) grows into 감동적인 (gamdongjeogin) = moving. One suffix, hundreds of instant adjectives.

target: 영화가 시작하기 전에 광고가 너무 많아요.
english: There are too many ads before the movie starts.
tip: -기 전에 (-gi jeone) = 'before': 시작하기 전에.

target: 저는 자막 없이 드라마를 이해하고 싶어요.
english: I want to understand dramas without subtitles.
tip: 없이 (eopsi) after a noun = 'without it': 자막 없이 (jamak eopsi) = without subtitles. It's the adverb form of 없다 (eopda = to not exist) – 'the subtitles not existing'.

target: 그 인기 드라마는 소설을 원작으로 해요.
english: That popular drama is based on a novel.
tip: 원작 (wonjak) = the original work: 소설을 원작으로 해요 (soseoreul wonjageuro haeyo) = takes the novel as its original. This is the set pattern for calling something an adaptation.

target: 저는 예고편만 보고도 눈물이 났어요.
english: I teared up just from the trailer.
tip: -고도 = 'even after / even just': 예고편만 보고도 (yegopyeonman bogodo) = even just from watching the trailer. It flags a result arriving earlier than expected – tears before the film.

target: 미술관 안에서는 사진을 찍으면 안 돼요.
english: You must not take photos inside the museum.
tip: 'Must not' is built from 'if': 찍으면 안 돼요 (jjigeumyeon an dwaeyo) is literally 'if you photograph, it won't do'. Korean bans things by condition, not command.

target: 그 특별 전시는 예약을 해야 볼 수 있어요.
english: You can only see that special exhibition with a reservation.
tip: -아/어야 means 'only if': 예약을 해야 볼 수 있어요 (yeyageul haeya bol su isseoyo) = only if you reserve can you see it. The condition ending itself carries the 'only'.

target: 할머니께서 판소리를 아주 좋아하세요.
english: My grandmother really loves pansori.
tip: Elder subject → 좋아하세요 (joahaseyo), the honorific present.

target: 공항에 세 시간 전에 도착했어요.
english: I arrived at the airport three hours early.
tip: Hours of duration use native numbers: 세 시간 (se sigan) = three hours.

target: 탑승권을 여기 보여 주세요.
english: Please show your boarding pass here.
tip: Chaining 주다 (juda = give) after a verb turns it into a favor for someone: 보여 주세요 (boyeo juseyo) = show it – for me. Korean marks who benefits right inside the verb.

target: 창가 자리로 부탁해요.
english: A window seat, please.
tip: (으)로 marks the choice: 창가 자리로 (changga jariro) = as a window seat.
